title: Spring Lecture #27: Spring JDBC Complete Tutorial

questions.question: Which statement about `javax.sql.DataSource` is correct?
options: A `DataSource` is itself one open database connection that all repositories share
Every `DataSource` is a connection pool, so `getConnection()` never creates a new physical connection
`DataSource` is an interface for obtaining connections; an implementation such as `HikariDataSource` may back it with a pool, but another may open a new connection per call
`DataSource` is a Spring class that replaces JDBC, so `Connection` and `PreparedStatement` are no longer used
questions.explanation: `DataSource` is only a connection-provider abstraction (`getConnection()`). Pooling depends on the implementation: HikariCP's `HikariDataSource` pools connections, while a simple implementation may create a new physical connection each time. Spring JDBC still uses `Connection`, `PreparedStatement` and `ResultSet` internally.

questions.question: A teammate is worried: "`JdbcTemplate` closes the connection after every query, so we pay the full TCP + authentication cost on every request." The app uses Spring Boot's default HikariCP `DataSource`. What actually happens on that `close()`?
options: The pool intercepts `close()` and returns the connection to the pool for reuse; the physical connection normally stays open
The physical connection is closed, and HikariCP reopens a new one in the background for the next request
`close()` is ignored entirely, so connections are never released and the pool eventually runs out
The connection is closed and the next query fails until the application is restarted
questions.explanation: With a pooled `DataSource`, the `Connection` handed out is a wrapper. Calling `close()` returns it to the pool, so later requests borrow an already-authenticated connection. The cost of creating physical connections is paid rarely, which is the main performance benefit of pooling.

questions.question: With the lecture's code, a client calls `GET /api/student/999`, and no student has id 999. There is no `@ControllerAdvice`. What happens?
options: 200 OK with an empty body, because `queryForObject()` returns `null` when no row matches
`queryForObject()` throws `EmptyResultDataAccessException`, which is not handled, so the client gets a 500 error
404 Not Found, because Spring maps an empty query result to 404 automatically
200 OK with a `Student` whose fields are all null or 0
questions.explanation: `queryForObject()` expects exactly one row: zero rows throw `EmptyResultDataAccessException` (more than one throws `IncorrectResultSizeDataAccessException`). It never returns null for a missing row, and Spring does not turn that exception into a 404 by itself. The notes show catching only `EmptyResultDataAccessException` to return `Optional.empty()`, or using `query(...)` with `findFirst()`.

questions.question: The `students` table contains exactly 3 rows. What does this print?
options: 1 2 3 | size=3
0 | size=3
3 | size=1
0 1 2 | size=3
questions.explanation: `JdbcTemplate.query()` iterates the `ResultSet` and calls the mapper once per row, passing a zero-based row number, so it prints 0, 1, 2. It collects the mapped objects into a list of size 3. The mapper converts only one row per call; Spring handles the iteration (and returns an empty list when there are no rows).

questions.question: A repository's `findById` wraps `queryForObject()` in `try { ... } catch (DataAccessException e) { return Optional.empty(); }`. During a MySQL outage, the API keeps answering "Student not found" instead of reporting an error. What is the right fix?
options: Catch only `EmptyResultDataAccessException` for the not-found case and let other `DataAccessException`s (such as `CannotGetJdbcConnectionException`) propagate
Catch `SQLException` instead, since `JdbcTemplate` rethrows the raw JDBC exception
Replace `Optional.empty()` with `null`, so callers can tell the difference
Increase `spring.datasource.hikari.connection-timeout` so the outage is never noticed
questions.explanation: `DataAccessException` is the root of Spring's whole data-access hierarchy. Catching it turns outages, bad SQL and constraint errors into a false 'not found'. Only `EmptyResultDataAccessException` means 'no row'. `JdbcTemplate` translates `SQLException` into unchecked `DataAccessException` subtypes, so catching `SQLException` would not even compile around it.

questions.question: The `students` table has `email ... UNIQUE`. `createStudent()` calls `jdbcTemplate.update(...)` with an email that already exists, and the method has no try/catch and no `throws` clause. Which statement is correct?
options: It does not compile, because the `SQLException` from the driver must be caught or declared
`update()` returns 0 and no exception is thrown, because the row was simply not inserted
Spring translates the driver's `SQLException` into `DuplicateKeyException`, an unchecked `DataAccessException` subtype, which propagates to the caller
Spring catches the error, logs it, and returns -1 to signal a constraint violation
questions.explanation: `JdbcTemplate` catches the checked, vendor-specific `SQLException` and translates it into Spring's unchecked hierarchy. A unique-key violation becomes `DuplicateKeyException` (a kind of `DataIntegrityViolationException`). No try/catch is required, and the service can convert it into a domain exception like `EmailAlreadyExistsException`.

questions.question: The table column was renamed from `name` to `full_name`. The `Student` class still has `setName(...)` (and `setId`, `setEmail`, `setAge`). What does the first student look like, assuming the row is `(1, 'Rohit Negi', 'rohit@gmail.com', 26)`?
options: Student{id=1, name='Rohit Negi', email='rohit@gmail.com', age=26}, because `full_name` is mapped to the closest property
Student{id=1, name='null', email='rohit@gmail.com', age=26}: `full_name` maps only to a `fullName` property, so `name` stays unpopulated
A `TypeMismatchException`, because the column count no longer matches the number of properties
An `IncorrectResultSizeDataAccessException`, because one column could not be mapped
questions.explanation: `BeanPropertyRowMapper` matches columns to setters by name, converting underscores to camelCase, so `full_name` would map to `setFullName`. `Student` has no such property, so the column is skipped and `name` stays null (`checkFullyPopulated` defaults to false, so there is no error). Aliasing the column (`full_name AS name`) or a custom `RowMapper` fixes it, which is the 'naming-convention dependence' limitation in the notes.

questions.question: The service has `spring.datasource.hikari.maximum-pool-size=10` and `connection-timeout=30000`. A slow report query (about 60 s) is triggered by 50 users at once. Requests start failing after about 30 s with a connection error, and even simple endpoints hang. What is happening, and what is the sound response?
options: HikariCP opens extra connections beyond the maximum under load, and MySQL rejects them; setting `minimum-idle=50` fixes it
The `connection-timeout` closes running queries after 30 s; raising it to 600000 is the fix
Each request receives its own pool, so 50 pools of 10 overwhelm MySQL; use `DriverManager` instead

All 10 connections are held by slow queries, so other requests wait for a free connection and fail after the 30 s timeout (`CannotGetJdbcConnectionException`); fix the slow query or isolate it, and size the pool from load tests rather than just making it huge
questions.explanation: The pool never exceeds its maximum, so request 11 onwards waits for a returned connection. `connection-timeout` is the maximum wait to BORROW a connection; it does not limit query time. Once it expires, Spring reports `CannotGetJdbcConnectionException`. A much larger pool just moves the overload to the database, so the notes advise sizing from concurrency, query duration, DB capacity and load tests.

questions.question: With the lecture's code, a client sends `PUT /api/student` with body `{"name":"Rohit","email":"rohit@gmail.com","age":26}` (no `id`). Student 8 exists. What happens?
options: A `NullPointerException` in the service, because `getId()` returns null
Student 8 is updated, because MySQL treats `WHERE id = NULL` as matching the most recent row
`id` is bound as SQL NULL, `WHERE id = NULL` matches no row, so "Updation failed" is printed, yet the client still receives 200 "DONE"
Spring throws `EmptyResultDataAccessException`, because the UPDATE affected zero rows
questions.explanation: `getId()` returns a null `Long` (passing it on is not dereferencing, so there is no NPE), and `JdbcTemplate` binds it as NULL. In SQL, `id = NULL` is never true, so the update count is 0 and the repository prints "Updation failed". `update()` does not throw for zero rows, and the lecture's controller ignores the result, so the client still gets 200 "DONE". The row count should drive the HTTP response, for example a 404.

questions.question: A team adds their own `@Bean public DataSource dataSource() { HikariDataSource ds = new HikariDataSource(); ds.setJdbcUrl(...); ds.setUsername(...); ds.setPassword(...); return ds; }`. Afterwards, `spring.datasource.hikari.maximum-pool-size=25` in `application.properties` seems to be ignored. Why?
options: When the application defines its own `DataSource` bean, Boot's datasource auto-configuration backs off, so the `spring.datasource.hikari.*` properties are not bound to this manually created instance
HikariCP ignores `maximum-pool-size` unless `minimum-idle` is set to the same value
`spring.datasource.hikari.*` properties apply only when `spring.datasource.driver-class-name` is set explicitly
Pool size can only be configured in `pom.xml`, not in `application.properties`
questions.explanation: Spring Boot creates and configures the `DataSource` (binding `spring.datasource.*` and `spring.datasource.hikari.*`) only if none is defined. A user-defined bean makes the auto-configuration back off, so this hand-built `HikariDataSource` gets only the values set in code. Either rely on auto-configuration or bind the properties to your bean yourself (for example with `@ConfigurationProperties`).
